title: refactor(enter): remove dashboard loading chatter
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes route-level loading cards and per-section loading messages; content appears as each request resolves.
- Keeps errors and feedback for explicit actions such as saving or deleting.
- Removes the now-unused placeholder code; no data fetching or API behavior changes.

Validation: Biome and git diff checks passed. Full frontend build will run in CI; this worktree has no installed dependencies.

gist.headline: Less waiting room, more dashboard
gist.blurb: The dashboard stopped narrating every tiny loading moment. Sections now quietly bloom into view as their data arrives, while save and delete actions still tell you when they need to.
gist.summary: Removed route-level loading cards, per-section loading messages, and unused dashboard placeholder code so Enter dashboard content renders independently as each request resolves, with explicit action feedback retained for saves and deletes.
gist.impact: Dashboard users will see account, keys, Pollen, models, activity, quests, and top-up content appear progressively without a layer of loading chatter, while actionable errors and confirmations remain visible.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden dashboard where several little panels bloom open naturally instead of being covered by loading cards. Polli, wearing a tiny gardener's hat, observes the calm progressive reveal beside a retro terminal; small code-plants and flowers represent independently arriving sections, while a clear save/checkmark sign remains for explicit actions.

Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, chunky retro sprites, warm lighting, lo-fi vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, nostalgic but beautiful, emotionally warm.
